verify: ed25519: verify `signature` (hex, 64 bytes) over the UTF-8 bytes of `canonical` using `public_key` (hex, raw 32-byte ed25519 point). `canonical` is the exact byte string that was signed — JSON with keys sorted lexicographically at every level and no insignificant whitespace (a subset of RFC 8785 / JCS). `payload` is the same object parsed; re-canonicalise it and you MUST reproduce `canonical`. If `payload.payment` is present it names the x402 payment that bought this response. On `payment.network`, find the `AuthorizationUsed(payer, nonce)` log emitted by `payment.asset`; in that same transaction receipt (not just the same block) require status 1 and a `Transfer(payer, payTo, amount)` log from `payment.asset`. Those arguments are the fields of `payment` with the same names.
rotation: Keys are rotated with notice. A replacement key is published in this document with `active: false` at least 30 days before it signs anything; at cutover it becomes `active: true` and the key it replaces stays listed with `active: false`, so attestations signed earlier can still be checked. A pinned verifier should add the announced key during that window. A key revoked for compromise is removed from this document immediately, without the 30-day notice.
